newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIAN REFINERY TO INCREASE OUTPUT BY YEAR 2005.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIAN REFINERY TO INCREASE OUTPUT BY YEAR 2005.

text.p: Bulgaria's biggest refinery Nefftohim will increase refined crude oil volumes by the year 2005 as a 4-5 percent rise in domestic petrol consumption is expected, refinery's executive director said on Thursday.
Stefan Nedelchev said annual refining volumes would rise to nine million tonnes from 7.5 million tonnes by the year 2005 after the cabinet approved on Thursday the refinery's long-term programme.
"We will achieve these volumes through technological reconstruction," Nedelchev told a news conference, quoted by the state news agency BTA.
Under the programme Neftohim will produce only unleaded petrol by the year 2005, while now the refinery produces just one type, which comprises 15-20 percent from the total output, he said.
Some $45 million will be invested for cutting sulpher content in the produced diesel and the refinery has already purchased a U.S. firm's license for the implementation of most modern technology.
Neftohim's management plans to set up joint ventures including for ethilene through attracting foreign capital, Nedelchev said.

The refinery, located at the Black Sea port of Bourgas, will invest some $130 million in modernisation projects by the year 2005. It is in a process of negotiating a World Bank loan to help finance them, BTA said.
